To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mobile recommender systems can be improved by using the web recommender system’s knowledge and that the web recommender systems can benefit by using the mobile recommender system’s features.

mobile recommender systems can be improved through the use of the following: (1) the use of mobile device features, (2) the use of social features and (3) the integration of mobile and web recommender systems.

the main differences between web and mobile recommendation systems are: the user context (e.g. user profile, user preferences, user location, user activity, user behavior), the item context (e.g., item popularity, item price, item availability, item rating, item reviews) and the context of the recommendation process (e.g. time, location, device).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the main differences between mobile and web recommender systems?

the identification of the factors that have been considered in the literature and the factors that have not yet been considered but should be included in the development of mobile recommender systems.
identifying and classifying the main concepts and factors that have an effect on mobile recommender system development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mobile recommender systems can be considered as a subdomain of the web recommendation domain and the research on mobile recommender algorithms should be considered as a research area within web recommendation algorithms.
there is a lack of a clear definition and a unified view of the concept of mobile recommender systems, which is a major problem in the development of mobile recommender technologies.
mobile recommender systems have been studied for more than a decade and there are several factors that have an influence on their design and performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identify the factors that have a significant impact on mobile recommenders, the main differences between web and mobile recommenders and we provide a list of future directions that can be followed by the research community in order to improve mobile recommender systems.
mobile recommender systems should be able to provide recommendations in different mobile environments.
mobile recommender systems can provide a wide range of benefits for both users and vendors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobile recommender systems can be seen as a sub-domain of the traditional recommender systems and the mobile environment can be seen as an extension of the web environment.
the mobile recommendation domain is still in its infancy, and there is a lot of work to be done in order to provide a more integrated mobile recommender systems domain.

mobile recommender systems should be considered as an independent field of research and that the current research should focus on the development of new algorithms for mobile recommender systems, the development of new interfaces that can be used in mobile environments and on the integration between the mobile and the web recommender systems.
